plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Measurement, Year 5 (VC2M5M04): estimate and construct angles in degrees with a protractor, including reflex angles
plan.shape: short cycles: estimate, then construct, then reflex, each modelled and tried straight away, because the three moves build on each other
plan.criticalFeature: estimate first against 90° and 180°, then measure; a reflex angle is 360° minus the inside angle
decisionPoints: the choice check on reflex angles
the hinge: find the reflex angle
plan.anchor: quarter turn 90°, half turn 180°, full turn 360°
plan.catchUp: Missed Session 1? Show the angle-names chart and model one measurement on the inner scale before the practice round.

manipulatives: A protractor and a ruler for every student
A large demonstration protractor, or the on-screen protractor
studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The anchor on the board: quarter turn 90°, half turn 180°, full turn 360°

example.prompt: Could 30° be a good estimate for an obtuse angle?

items.prompt: Mia estimated 30° for an angle that measures 150°. What mistake might she have made?
items.answer: She judged the wrong side or confused acute and obtuse; 150° is more than 90°, so it cannot be about 30°.

items.prompt: Why can't you measure a reflex angle straight away with a 180° protractor? How do you find it instead?
items.answer: The protractor only reaches 180°; measure the inside angle and subtract it from 360°.

slides.notes: Open Session 2 of the angles week. One line: today we estimate angles, draw them, and measure the big ones.
Prep slide. Protractor, ruler and a sharp pencil for every student. Print the Worksheet for all, and some Extension and Supported Worksheet copies.

slides.title: Decimal to fraction
prompts: Write 0.4 as a fraction in its simplest form.

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with fractions, decimals and percentages again.
ASK: Write 0.4 as a fraction in its simplest form.
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 2/5. ACCEPT: 4/10 then simplified
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, move on.
Less -> write 4/10, divide top and bottom by 2 together, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Four tenths simplifies to two fifths. Tick or fix.
trap: stopping at 4/10.
Fix: ask what divides both numbers, student simplifies.
notes.prep: Daily Review from Term 3 Week 9. Whole block under 6 minutes.

beats: ASK: What is 10% of 350?
15 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: 35
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, move on.
Less -> 10% is one tenth: share 350 into 10 equal parts, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 35. One tenth of 350. Tick or fix.
trap: writing 3.5 or 350.
Fix: say ten percent is one tenth, student divides by 10.
notes.prep: Term 3 Week 9 retrieval: percentage of an amount.

beats: ASK: What is one fifth plus three tenths?
30 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: 5/10 or 1/2
SCAN boards for a common denominator.
80%+ -> reveal, then Fluency.
Less -> rename one fifth as two tenths on the strips, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: One fifth is two tenths, so five tenths, which is one half. Tick or fix.
trap: adding across to get 4/15.
Fix: rename to tenths first, student re-adds.
notes.prep: Spaced retrieval from Term 3 Week 8: adding related fractions.

slides.title: Add with the written method: 3 digits

beats: SAY: Now the written method. Line up the places and start with the ones.
ASK: Solve it with the written method.
30 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: 923
SCAN boards for the regrouped digits.
80%+ -> reveal, next one.
Less -> model the ones and the regroup together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 923. Tick or fix, and check every regroup.
trap: forgetting to add a regrouped ten.
Fix: circle each carried digit, student re-adds that column.
notes.prep: Algorithm fluency: 3 digits, then 4, then 5. Whole block under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Add with the written method: 4 digits

beats: SAY: Now 4 digits. Same method, one more column.
ASK: Solve it with the written method.
45 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: 8 043
SCAN boards for the regrouped digits.
80%+ -> reveal, next one.
Less -> model the ones and the regroup together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 8 043. Tick or fix, and check every regroup.
trap: forgetting to add a regrouped ten.
Fix: circle each carried digit, student re-adds that column.

slides.title: Add with the written method: 5 digits

beats: SAY: Now 5 digits. Same method, one more column.
ASK: Solve it with the written method.
60 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: 84 403
SCAN boards for the regrouped digits.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> model the ones and the regroup together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 84 403. Tick or fix, and check every regroup.
trap: forgetting to add a regrouped ten.
Fix: circle each carried digit, student re-adds that column.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to estimate angles and draw them accurately with a protractor.
successCriteria: I can estimate an angle using 90° and 180° as guides.
I can draw an angle of a given size with a ruler and protractor.
I can find a reflex angle by measuring the inside angle and subtracting from 360°.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Yesterday we measured angles. Today we estimate them, draw them, and find big ones.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: Estimating comes first, drawing is our big goal.
Reflex angles are the challenge.
notes.prep: SC1 estimating is reachable for all; SC2 drawing an angle is the core; SC3 reflex angles is the exit evidence and the stretch.

slides.title: Name it, then estimate it
slides.prompt: Is it closer to 90° or to 180°?

beats: POINT to the angle.
SAY: Here's an angle. First we name it, then we have a go at its size.
ASK: What is this angle called?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: obtuse
ASK: Closer to 90 or to 180? Write your estimate.
15 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: closer to 180, about 140
SCAN boards for estimates between 120 and 160.
80%+ -> praise the reasoning, move on.
Less -> hold up a book corner and a ruler edge, compare, re-ask.
trap: estimating under 90 for an obtuse angle.
Fix: name it first, student re-estimates above 90.
notes.prep: Launch after the LI retrieves Session 1 names and starts benchmark estimating. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: A careful guess using what you know.
slides.example: It is a bit more than a right angle, so about 100°.

notes.answer: a careful guess using what you know
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Estimate. Say it with me. Estimate.
SAY: An estimate is a careful guess.
For angles, we use a quarter turn and a half turn to help.
ASK: Is 100° a good estimate for a right angle?
10 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs sideways, close but a right angle is 90
trap: treating an estimate as a wild guess.
Fix: ask which benchmark it is near, student re-estimates.
notes.prep: Estimating keeps measurements honest: a reading that is far from the estimate means the wrong scale.

slides.title: Estimate, then measure
steps: It is more than 90° and less than 180°.
About a third of the way from 90° to 180°: about 120°.

beats: MODEL comparing with a square corner.
SAY: It's more than a quarter turn, but well short of a half turn.
POINT between 90 and 180.
SAY: It's about a third of the way along, so I estimate 120.
ASK: Read the protractor. How close was my estimate?
15 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: 118
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 118 degrees. My estimate of 120 tells me I read the right scale.
trap: reading 62 on the other scale.
Fix: compare with the estimate, student re-reads.
notes.stretch: Estimate three angles in the room, then measure them.
notes.help: Say quarter turn or half turn first, then estimate.
notes.prep: Estimating is a check on measuring: far from the estimate means the wrong scale. SC1.

slides.title: Draw an angle of 70°
steps: Rule an arm and mark the vertex.
Centre on the vertex, 0 on the arm.
Count up from that 0 and dot at 70.
Rule from the vertex through the dot.

beats: MODEL the arm and the vertex dot.
SAY: I start with one straight arm and a dot for the corner.
MODEL the centre and the 0.
SAY: Centre on the dot, and the 0 sits on my arm.
ASK: Which scale do I count along to reach 70?
10 sec. Cue: voices off. Point... now.
EXPECT: pointing to the inner scale
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: The one that starts at 0 on my arm. Dot at 70, rule through.
trap: dotting at 110 on the other scale.
Fix: check it looks acute, student redraws.
notes.stretch: Draw 70° on an arm pointing left.
notes.prep: Drawing is measuring in reverse: same centre, same 0. SC2.

beats: POINT to the big arc.
SAY: This angle goes the long way round. My protractor stops at 180.
MODEL measuring the inside angle.
SAY: So I measure the small angle inside instead. It's 60 degrees.
ASK: A full turn is 360. What is the reflex angle?
15 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: 300
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 360 take away 60 is 300 degrees.
trap: subtracting from 180 to get 120.
Fix: point to the full turn on the anchor, student redoes.
notes.stretch: Why do the inside angle and the reflex angle always make 360?
notes.help: Write 360 - ___ = ___ and fill in the inside angle.
notes.prep: The anchor does the work: a full turn is 360. SC3.

slides.title: Find the reflex angle
slides.prompt: The inside angle is 50°. What is the reflex angle?

options.misconception: gives the inside angle, not the reflex angle

beats: SAY: Three answers. Only one uses a full turn.
ASK: The inside angle is 50. What is the reflex angle?
15 sec. Cue: voices off. Point... now.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call one child: why not A?
Less -> draw it: shade the small angle, trace the long way round, re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: B. 360 take away 50 is 310.
trap: pointing to A.
Fix: ask how far a full turn goes, student redoes 360 - 50.
notes.prep: First decision point, on the step most students skip. Under 80% means rebuild with the demonstration protractor.

slides.title: Estimate first
slides.ask: Estimate this angle. Write your estimate.
slides.pivot: compare with a book corner and a ruler edge together
slides.followUp: cold call one board: which guide did you use?

items.say: 240 degrees. It is reflex: more than a half turn. Tick or fix.

say: Write your best estimate on your board.
trap: estimates on the wrong side of 90.
Fix: name the angle first, then estimate.
notes.help: Say smaller than, about, or bigger than a quarter turn.
notes.prep: Guided estimating: accept within about 10°. Reflex item tests the half-turn benchmark. SC1.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you. The inside angle is marked.
ASK: What is the reflex angle marked with the question mark?
20 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: 320
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> trace the full turn with a finger: 360 all the way round, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 320 degrees. 360 take away 40. Tick or fix.
trap: writing 140.
Fix: ask what a full turn is, student subtracts from 360.
notes.prep: The hinge before independence. Students writing 140 start with the teacher on the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Estimate, draw and measure the angles on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: When you finish, the early finisher option is the Extension.
Say the steps with me. Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE. Check drawn angles with your own protractor.
TIME 20 minutes. Check-in at question 10.
trap: drawing from the wrong 0.
Fix: check against the estimate, student redraws.
notes.stretch: Extension: build triangles from angles, and reflex riddles.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: protractors printed on, and hints.
notes.prep: Independent practice: estimate, draw, reflex, worded and reasoning questions. Sheet is evidence for SC1 to SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Draw an angle of 125° on your board.

notes.answer: an obtuse angle of 125°. An acute angle means the wrong scale (55°)
beats: SAY: Last one. Use your protractor and draw it on your board.
ASK: Draw an angle of 125 degrees.
60 sec. Cue: boards up on cue.
EXPECT: an obtuse angle, about 125
RECORD who draws an acute angle: the wrong scale.
They start tomorrow's check with the teacher.
trap: drawing 55°.
Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: an acute drawing shows the scale error at a glance. Drives tomorrow's grouping.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner how estimating helps you measure.

notes.answer: open - listen for checking the reading against the estimate
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can draw an angle?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with an acute drawing matters most.
ASK: Tell your partner how estimating helps you measure.
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: it shows if I read the wrong scale
notes.prep: Self-assessment read beside the exit evidence. SC2.
